text: 'Puget Sound on the Pacific Coast' by Albert Beirstadt
moreInfo: According to the Seattle Art Museum, Beirstadt painted this in 1870 without having been to the Puget Sound. Nonetheless, I love the drama and granduer of it all.
I first saw this painting while visiting the MET with my mom. I love how it feels like Mäda's stoic expression and assured stance contrasts the colorful smudginess of her dress and surroundings.

text: Map of the French invasion of Russia by Charles Minard
moreInfo: I first saw this map in Ed Tufte's book on quantitative data. He claims Minard's visualization of Napolean's campaign 'may well be the best statistical graphic ever drawn'

text: Isochrone of the Melbourne railway system 1910–1922
moreInfo: I found this image while reading the Wikipedia page for Isochrones. As a causal fan of public transportation, I loved the idea being visualized. Plus, the colors and aesthetics are really nice.
